title: The Bigger Picture — Daily AI Analysis
paragraphs: A deeper look at today's Bigger Picture card: what is moving the market, and what to watch. The Full Report carries the full analysis.

What moves the market today. Fact: Bloomberg reports that Taiwan's main index is up 72 percent this year, the best of more than 90 it tracks, because its AI earnings come from chip sales rather than memory prices. Fact: the research firm Dell'Oro says data centre spending rose 92 percent in the second quarter, and Lisa Su, chief executive of the chipmaker AMD, says demand for its AI chips still exceeds what it can make.

Fact: more of the build is borrowed. The Financial Times reports, citing unnamed sources, that SpaceX, which now includes xAI, seeks about $40 billion in loans and bonds for Nvidia chips, and the Wall Street Journal reports that the cloud company Lambda is raising up to $4 billion on orders that rest largely on one customer, Anthropic. Fact: Bloomberg reports that Ray Dalio, founder of Bridgewater, one of the world's biggest hedge funds, called AI a "classic bubble" that is "close" to bursting, citing heavy borrowing and rising interest rates, while Larry Fink, chief executive of BlackRock, one of the world's biggest fund managers, told NBC News he fears losing the AI race more than a bubble.

Our view: chip demand is still measured in orders, the build now runs on debt, and the biggest money managers disagree about which risk is larger. All of them name the interest rate, so the coming inflation data and rate decisions matter to AI more than usual. On the ground, the limit has moved from chips to electricity and consent: Google now pays the whole power bill for its new sites, while Heatmap counts $260 billion of US projects cancelled after local opposition.

What to watch and follow. 1. 13 October: JPMorgan Chase reports; its chief executive Jamie Dimon says AI cyber risk rose tenfold, so watch for AI losses or lending pulled back. 2. 14 October: US inflation for September; a hot number makes borrowed AI money dearer. 3. 15 October: TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, reports; a raised outlook confirms the boom is in orders, a flat one is the first crack. 4. 27 to 29 October: the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank decide rates, and Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon are expected to report the same days (dates estimated, not announced); their spending plans decide whether the 92 percent continues. 5. 6 November: the US jobs report, the first measured check on cuts that name AI, after FICO and HubSpot this week.
Unknowns. The SpaceX and Lambda figures come from unnamed sources and a private letter, Heatmap's count is unchecked, and the price Google pays for its nuclear power is secret.
This is analysis of the news, not financial advice or an investment recommendation.
